title: Fast integrate: 7-day crew sprint and evidence wallet
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight, practical plan for converting an accepted hire (IC or contractor) into a productive, evidence-backed teammate inside 7 calendar days. Focus is speed + low friction: minimize meetings, maximize observable outputs, and create an "evidence wallet" that documents signals for managers and hiring panels. Intended for: new ICs (engineer, infra, platform) and hiring managers running conversion or rapid onboarding paths.

Goals (primary):
- Deliver 3 small, reviewable artifacts the new hire completes in week 1 that demonstrate access, code, and collaboration.
- Create a repeatable mentor handoff ritual that reduces manager cognitive load.
- Produce a compact evidence wallet (1 page) for calibration and probation review.

Non-goals:
- Exhaustive orientation checklist (this doc links to those).
- Full product deep dives. Keep it tactical.

Quick timeline (7 calendar days)
Day 0 (pre-start - HR + manager prep)
- Confirm accounts provisioned: okta, slack, Google Drive, infra read-only. Note any exceptions (private-deployments reqs).
- Manager creates a single PR template repo (private) with three "first-7 tasks" issues.
- Mentor assigned (peer IC, not manager). Mentor receives a short brief: goals, expected time budget (3-4 hours over 7 days), and the evidence wallet template.
- Hiring coms: welcome email with one-liner schedule and links.

Day 1 (launch)
- 30 min async kickoff: one slide with team mission, repo links, meeting norms. No >30m live call unless critical.
- Task A assigned: local dev setup + smoke test. Outcome: one PR that updates README with reproducible local start steps and a recorded 90s terminal output snippet.
- Mentor check-in: 30m paired setup session (can be recorded).

Day 2-3 (deliver green builds + code)
- Task B: small bugfix or integration smoke that touches the serving runtime or infra infra test harness. Outcome: small PR (<= 10 lines) with linked unit test or e2e check.
- Task C: write one short doc (1-pager) describing a key failure mode observed during local runs and a suggested mitigation or hint for future hires. Add to evidence wallet.
- Mentor does code review of Task A/B with explicit 3-point rubric (see below). First comments should be in-line within 24 hrs.

Day 4-5 (collaborate + visibility)
- Join 1 async triage thread (observability or ops) and add one constructive comment or repro. Outcome: slack thread link plus short note in evidence wallet.
- Optional: shadow-call 30m with product/ops owner if learning is cross-functional.

Day 6 (wrap-up)
- Ship final PR that stitches previous changes into a tiny integration test or CI job that runs smoke.
- Manager + mentor quick readout (15m) for signals and blocker removal. No status deck.

Day 7 (evidence wallet and reflection)
- New hire fills the evidence wallet (template below) and shares with manager + hiring panel.
- Manager completes a short calibration note (recommended next steps: training, ownership, IC pitch).

Evidence wallet (1 page) - required fields (use bulletized answers)
- Name / role / start date
- 3 artifacts shipped (title + link)
- Short rubric scores (skill, autonomy, communication) with one-line reasoning
- Top 2 blockers encountered and remediation steps taken
- Mentor notes (2 lines): what went well, what to prioritize next 30 days
- Suggested first 30-day micro-ownership

Mentor 3-point code review rubric (applies to Task A/B)
- Correctness: PR does what it says, tests/smoke pass (yes/no)
- Clarity: commit message + PR description explain WHY, not only WHAT (scale: 1-3)
- Collaborativeness: candidate responds to review comments constructively and updates PR within 48h (scale: 1-3)
Use numeric scoring (e.g., correctness: pass, clarity:2, collaborativeness:3) and write 1 short sentence justification.

Hiring manager probes (sample questions for 15m readout)
- What surprised you about the codebase in day 1?
- Which tiny piece of the product would you adopt as your first measurable ownerable?
- What support do you need to move from triage to independent delivery?

Acceptance and communication timeline (post-offer -> day 0)
- Offer accepted: send pre-start folder with links + mentor name within 24h.
- 3 days pre-start: confirm IAM groups and special VPN/PM network access.
- Day 0 morning: short manager note (2–3 bullets) with expectations. Keep comms plain.

Risk signals (escalate early)
- No PRs within 72 hours and no evidence of local environment progress (mentor checked). Suggest remedial pairing or extended ramp.
- Repeated inability to run even smoke tests after mentor pairing: schedule SRE/infra assist.
- No response to asynchronous messages for >48h during week 1: manager ping + people-ops check-in.

Conversion-specific additions (contractor -> perm)
- Add 1 extra artifact: a short migration plan for one area the contractor touched (knowledge transfer demo).
- Evidence wallet should explicitly answer: why should we convert this hire? Provide 3 signals (technical, collaboration, ramp speed).
- HR: attach contractor contract reference and timeline for conversion review (usually 30–45 days).

Templates and sample phrasing (copy/paste)
- Mentor intro Slack: "hi @NAME — I’m your mentor for week 1. Expect 3 small tasks, pairing sessions on day1 and day3, and a short evidence wallet on day7. Ping me in #team-mentor for quick help."
- Manager day 0 note: "Welcome! Primary outcome for week1: one merged PR, one doc, one CI job. I’ll meet 15m day6. Be bold, ask early."

Fast checklist (for manager before start)
- [ ] Mentor assigned and briefed
- [ ] Repo + 3 starter issues created
- [ ] Accounts provisioned and admin slack invites sent
- [ ] Evidence wallet template copied to new hire drive folder

Integration with existing artifacts
- Link to global onboarding index: CONFLUENCE:Onboard/index
- If private deployments involved, see preboard checklist: CONFLUENCE:Security/private-preboard
- Ticket template (Jira): JIRA:ENG-templates/first-7-tasks

Open questions / TODOs
- Evaluate whether 2 calendar days per task is too aggressive for non-engineer roles (PM, Research Ops) — propose an alternate 10-day micro-sprint for non-coders.
- Add a short micro-training (20m) on Redwood inference runtime internals for infra hires; need SME to record.

Notes to self (author):
- This format works best for product-path ICs; adapt language if hiring managers prefer live onboarding. Keep evidence wallet mandatory for conversion cases.

Appendix: short evidence-wallet template (copy into Drive)
- Header: name | role | start date
- Artifacts shipped: (1) link — short description (2) link — short description (3) link — short description
- Rubric: skill: x/3, autonomy: x/3, comms: x/3, 1-line justification
- Mentor 2-line summary, manager 1-line recommendation

End of doc.
